visibility.label: Clearly visible on a conventional karyotype
Sometimes visible; smaller cases often need FISH or a microarray
Usually not visible by arranging a conventional karyotype
Visible when the change is large; smaller cases often need FISH or a microarray

changes.label: An entire extra chromosome is present

diseases.teaching_notes: Down syndrome is the disease. Free trisomy 21, Robertsonian translocation, and mosaicism are different cytogenetic cases. The simple lab uses free trisomy 21 only.

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: free trisomy 21.
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: Three separate chromosome 21s
cytogenetic_cases.partner_note: None. The extra chromosome is free.
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not modify the shape or banding of chromosome 21. Robertsonian and mosaic Down syndrome are different cases.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: Three separate chromosome 21s
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Aneuploidy: free trisomy 21

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: Robertsonian translocation Down syndrome.
cytogenetic_cases.homolog_affected: A Robertsonian derivative plus extra chromosome 21 material
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: Extra chromosome 21 material is attached through a Robertsonian derivative
cytogenetic_cases.material_added: Chromosome 21 long-arm material on the derivative, with an additional 21
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not draw this as three free chromosomes 21.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: The cell does not simply contain three separate chromosomes 21
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Structural rearrangement producing trisomy 21 material

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: mosaic trisomy 21.
cytogenetic_cases.homolog_affected: Trisomy 21 in some cells and two chromosomes 21 in other cells
cytogenetic_cases.whole_chromosome_count: 47 in the trisomic line and 46 in the other line
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: One metaphase cannot show both lines
cytogenetic_cases.material_added: An extra chromosome 21 in the trisomic line only
cytogenetic_cases.partner_note: None. The extra chromosome in the trisomic line is free.
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not use one metaphase as the whole diagnosis.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: A second cell line has to be examined
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Mosaic free trisomy 21

references.label: NCBI Bookshelf
references.citation: Pal A, Daley SF. Down syndrome. StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing; 2026. Bookshelf ID NBK526016. Free trisomy 21, Robertsonian translocation, and mosaicism.

references.label: MedlinePlus Genetics
references.citation: Down syndrome. Most cases are trisomy 21. Translocation and mosaic Down syndrome are less common.

references.label: Clinical
references.citation: Bull MJ; Committee on Genetics. Health supervision for children with Down syndrome. Pediatrics. 2011;128(2):393-406.

references.citation: McGowan-Jordan J, Hastings RJ, Moore S, eds. ISCN 2020: An International System for Human Cytogenomic Nomenclature. Basel: Karger; 2020.

diseases.teaching_notes: Edwards syndrome is the disease. The simple lab uses complete trisomy 18. Mosaic trisomy 18 and partial trisomy 18 are different cases.

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: complete trisomy 18.
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: Three separate chromosome 18s
cytogenetic_cases.partner_note: None. The extra chromosome is free.
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not change the structure of chromosome 18.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: Three separate chromosome 18s
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Aneuploidy: free trisomy 18

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: mosaic trisomy 18.
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: One metaphase cannot show both lines
cytogenetic_cases.material_added: An extra chromosome 18 in the trisomic line only
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not treat one cell as every cell.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: A second cell line has to be examined
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Mosaic trisomy 18

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: partial trisomy 18.
cytogenetic_cases.homolog_affected: Extra chromosome 18 material, not a third free chromosome 18
cytogenetic_cases.specific_region: A segment of chromosome 18; the segment depends on the rearrangement
cytogenetic_cases.typical_configuration: Extra 18 material on a derivative chromosome
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: Not three separate chromosomes 18
cytogenetic_cases.partner_note: A partner chromosome is often involved, and it is not the same in every patient
example_notation: The ISCN depends on which segment of chromosome 18 is extra and how it is attached
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not draw three free chromosomes 18 for this case.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: The cell does not contain three intact chromosomes 18
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Partial trisomy 18

references.label: NCBI Bookshelf
references.citation: Trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome). StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing. Bookshelf ID NBK570597. Complete trisomy 18 is the common form; mosaic and partial trisomy 18 also occur.

references.label: MedlinePlus Genetics
references.citation: Trisomy 18. Mosaic trisomy 18 and partial trisomy 18 are described separately from complete trisomy 18.

references.label: ISCN
references.citation: McGowan-Jordan J, Hastings RJ, Moore S, eds. ISCN 2020: An International System for Human Cytogenomic Nomenclature. Basel: Karger; 2020.

diseases.teaching_notes: Patau syndrome is the disease. The simple lab uses complete trisomy 13. Robertsonian, mosaic, and partial forms are different cases.

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: complete trisomy 13.
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: Three separate chromosome 13s
cytogenetic_cases.partner_note: None. The extra chromosome is free.
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not change the structure of chromosome 13, and do not draw the Robertsonian form as three free chromosomes 13.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: Three separate chromosome 13s
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Aneuploidy: free trisomy 13

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: Robertsonian translocation trisomy 13.
cytogenetic_cases.homolog_affected: A Robertsonian derivative plus extra chromosome 13 material
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: Extra chromosome 13 material is carried on a Robertsonian derivative
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not draw this as three free chromosomes 13.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: The cell does not simply contain three separate chromosomes 13
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Structural rearrangement producing trisomy 13 material

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: mosaic trisomy 13.
cytogenetic_cases.whole_chromosome_count: 47 in the trisomic line and 46 in the other line
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: One metaphase cannot show both lines
cytogenetic_cases.material_added: An extra chromosome 13 in the trisomic line only
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not report one cell as the whole karyotype.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: A second cell line has to be examined
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Mosaic trisomy 13

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: partial trisomy 13.
cytogenetic_cases.homolog_affected: Extra chromosome 13 material, not a third free chromosome 13
cytogenetic_cases.specific_region: A segment of chromosome 13; the segment depends on the rearrangement
cytogenetic_cases.typical_configuration: Extra 13 material without three free chromosomes 13
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: Not three separate chromosomes 13
cytogenetic_cases.partner_note: A partner chromosome may be involved
example_notation: The ISCN depends on which segment of chromosome 13 is extra
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not draw three free chromosomes 13 for this case.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: The cell does not contain three intact chromosomes 13
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Partial trisomy 13

references.label: NCBI Bookshelf
references.citation: Siddik AB, Daley SF. Trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome). StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing; 2026. Bookshelf ID NBK559091. Complete, translocation, partial, and mosaic forms.

references.label: MedlinePlus Genetics
references.citation: Trisomy 13. Translocation trisomy 13 and mosaic trisomy 13 are distinguished from complete trisomy 13.

references.label: ISCN
references.citation: McGowan-Jordan J, Hastings RJ, Moore S, eds. ISCN 2020: An International System for Human Cytogenomic Nomenclature. Basel: Karger; 2020.

diseases.teaching_notes: Turner syndrome is the disease. 45,X is the canonical case. Mosaic 45,X/46,XX, an X isochromosome, a ring X, and other structural X abnormalities are different cases.

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: 45,X.
cytogenetic_cases.homolog_affected: A single X chromosome and no second sex chromosome
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: One sex chromosome, an X
cytogenetic_cases.partner_note: None. The second sex chromosome is absent.
cytogenetic_cases.mechanism: Sex-chromosome nondisjunction or anaphase loss producing a 45,X line
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not teach Turner syndrome as only a missing X. Mosaic and structural X cases exist.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: Only one X is present
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Monosomy X: 45,X

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: mosaic Turner syndrome.
cytogenetic_cases.homolog_affected: 45,X in some cells and a second line with two X chromosomes
cytogenetic_cases.whole_chromosome_count: 45 in one line and 46 in another
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: One metaphase cannot show both lines
cytogenetic_cases.material_missing: A sex chromosome in the 45,X line only
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not report one cell as the whole karyotype.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: A second cell line has to be examined
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Mosaic Turner syndrome, commonly 45,X/46,XX

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: a structural abnormality of one X chromosome.
cytogenetic_cases.specific_region: Example: isochromosome Xq, i(X)(q10). Other structural X abnormalities also occur.
cytogenetic_cases.structural_class: Isochromosome or other structural change of X
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: One X is structurally abnormal rather than simply absent
cytogenetic_cases.material_missing: Depends on the rearrangement. An i(X)(q10) lacks a normal Xp.
cytogenetic_cases.material_added: Depends on the rearrangement. An i(X)(q10) has two Xq arms.
cytogenetic_cases.partner_note: The second sex chromosome is the structurally abnormal X, not a Y in the usual example
cytogenetic_cases.mechanism: Structural abnormality of X with loss of some X material
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not draw this as 45,X.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: The X homologs are not a normal pair, and the count is not 45
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Turner syndrome from a structural X abnormality, example 46,X,i(X)(q10)

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: a ring X chromosome.
cytogenetic_cases.homolog_affected: One X is a ring chromosome
cytogenetic_cases.specific_region: Both ends of the X can be lost when the ring forms
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: One sex chromosome is a ring, not simply absent
cytogenetic_cases.material_missing: Material from one or both ends of the X, depending on the ring
cytogenetic_cases.mechanism: Ring X with loss of some X material
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not draw this as 45,X.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: A sex chromosome is present but is not a normal X
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Turner syndrome from a ring X

references.label: NCBI Bookshelf
references.citation: Shankar Kikkeri N, Nagalli S. Turner syndrome. StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing. Bookshelf ID NBK554621. About 40% to 50% of cases are 45,X; mosaic and structural X forms make up the rest.

references.label: Clinical
references.citation: Gravholt CH, et al. Clinical practice guidelines for the care of girls and women with Turner syndrome. Eur J Endocrinol. 2017;177(3):G1-G70.

references.label: ISCN
references.citation: McGowan-Jordan J, Hastings RJ, Moore S, eds. ISCN 2020. Basel: Karger; 2020. Section on mosaicism and clone size notation.

diseases.teaching_notes: Klinefelter syndrome is the disease. 47,XXY is the canonical case. Mosaic 46,XY/47,XXY and rarer higher-order sex-chromosome aneuploidies are different cases.

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: 47,XXY.
cytogenetic_cases.homolog_affected: Two X chromosomes and one Y chromosome
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: Two X chromosomes and one Y chromosome
cytogenetic_cases.partner_note: X and Y are both present. Neither is a translocation partner.
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not alter the banding of X or Y.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: The sex-chromosome complement is XXY
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Sex-chromosome trisomy: 47,XXY

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: mosaic 47,XXY.
cytogenetic_cases.homolog_affected: An XXY line and at least one other sex-chromosome line
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: One metaphase cannot show both lines
cytogenetic_cases.material_added: An extra X in the 47,XXY line
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not report one cell as the whole karyotype.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: A second cell line has to be examined
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Mosaic Klinefelter syndrome

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: a higher-order complement such as 48,XXXY.
cytogenetic_cases.homolog_affected: More than two X chromosomes, with a Y
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: More sex chromosomes than XXY
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not use 47,XXY as this karyotype.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: The sex-chromosome count is higher than XXY
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Higher-order Klinefelter karyotype, example 48,XXXY

references.label: NCBI Bookshelf
references.citation: Kadam SJ, Leslie SW, Ford GA. Klinefelter syndrome. StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing. Bookshelf ID NBK482314. 47,XXY is the common karyotype; mosaic and higher-order forms are less common.

references.label: NCBI PMC
references.citation: Bonomi M, Rochira V, Pasquali D, et al. Klinefelter syndrome (KS): genetics, clinical phenotype and hypogonadism. J Endocrinol Invest. 2016. A 47,XXY karyotype is present in 80–90% of cases.

references.label: Clinical
references.citation: Groth KA, Skakkebaek A, Host C, Gravholt CH, Bojesen A. Clinical review: Klinefelter syndrome—a clinical update. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2013;98(1):20-30.

references.label: ISCN
references.citation: McGowan-Jordan J, Hastings RJ, Moore S, eds. ISCN 2020: An International System for Human Cytogenomic Nomenclature. Basel: Karger; 2020.

diseases.teaching_notes: Cri-du-chat syndrome is the disease. The simple lab uses a terminal 5p deletion and does not pretend every patient has the same breakpoint. Interstitial 5p deletions and unbalanced rearrangements are different cases.

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: terminal deletion of 5p.
cytogenetic_cases.specific_region: Distal 5p, with critical regions around 5p15. Exact breakpoints vary.
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: One chromosome 5 has a shortened p arm
cytogenetic_cases.partner_note: None for the canonical simple deletion case
cytogenetic_cases.mechanism: Terminal deletion of one chromosome 5 short arm
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not assign one breakpoint to every patient. Deletion size varies. Interstitial deletions and unbalanced rearrangements are different cases.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: The chromosome 5 homologs differ in p-arm length
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Partial monosomy 5p

representative_teaching_karyotype.label: Female terminal 5p deletion; breakpoint not fixed

generation.structural_alteration: shorten the p arm of one chromosome 5

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: an unbalanced rearrangement that deletes 5p.
cytogenetic_cases.homolog_affected: A derivative chromosome that is missing distal 5p
cytogenetic_cases.specific_region: Distal 5p, with breakpoints that depend on the rearrangement
cytogenetic_cases.structural_class: Partial monosomy from an unbalanced rearrangement
cytogenetic_cases.typical_configuration: Derivative chromosome rather than a simple terminal deletion
cytogenetic_cases.whole_chromosome_count: Usually 46, sometimes 45 if a chromosome is lost
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: Chromosome 5 material is rearranged, not only shortened as an isolated deletion
cytogenetic_cases.material_added: Material from the partner chromosome may be present on the derivative
cytogenetic_cases.partner_note: A partner chromosome is involved, but it is not the same partner in every patient
example_notation: Unbalanced rearrangement deleting distal 5p; the ISCN depends on the partner and the breakpoints
cytogenetic_cases.mechanism: Unbalanced rearrangement involving chromosome 5 that produces monosomy 5p
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not build this as an isolated del(5p).
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: A second chromosome may also be derivative
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Partial monosomy 5p from an unbalanced rearrangement

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: an interstitial deletion within 5p.
cytogenetic_cases.specific_region: An internal segment of 5p, not necessarily a terminal deletion
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: The p arm may look less obviously shortened than a large terminal deletion
example_notation: 46,XX,del(5)(p) with two breakpoints; the bands are case-dependent
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not draw this as the terminal teaching deletion.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: Material is missing inside 5p rather than only from the end
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Partial monosomy 5p from an interstitial deletion

references.label: NCBI Bookshelf
references.citation: Cri du chat syndrome. StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing. Bookshelf ID NBK482460. Most cases are terminal 5p deletions; interstitial deletions and unbalanced rearrangements also occur. Critical regions are described in 5p15.

references.label: Clinical
references.citation: Nguyen JM, Qualmann KJ, Okashah R, Reilly A, Alexeyev MF, Campbell DJ. 5p deletions: current knowledge and future directions. Am J Med Genet C Semin Med Genet. 2015;169(3):224-238.

references.label: ISCN
references.citation: McGowan-Jordan J, Hastings RJ, Moore S, eds. ISCN 2020: An International System for Human Cytogenomic Nomenclature. Basel: Karger; 2020.

diseases.teaching_notes: Wolf-Hirschhorn syndrome is the disease. The simple lab uses a large terminal 4p deletion. Visibility is size-dependent: a small 4p16.3 deletion may not be obvious on a conventional karyotype. Unbalanced rearrangements are a different case.

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: terminal deletion of 4p.
cytogenetic_cases.specific_region: Distal 4p, key region 4p16.3. Exact breakpoint is case-dependent.
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: One chromosome 4 has a shortened p arm
cytogenetic_cases.partner_note: None for the canonical simple deletion case
cytogenetic_cases.mechanism: Terminal deletion of one chromosome 4 short arm
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not treat a small 4p16.3 deletion as this visible teaching karyotype. Small deletions can require FISH or a microarray.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: The chromosome 4 homologs differ in p-arm length
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Partial monosomy 4p

representative_teaching_karyotype.label: Female terminal 4p deletion; exact breakpoint case-dependent

generation.structural_alteration: remove distal p-arm material from one chromosome 4

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: a 4p deletion that is not the large terminal teaching example.
cytogenetic_cases.homolog_affected: One chromosome 4, or a derivative that deletes 4p16.3
cytogenetic_cases.specific_region: Critical region in 4p16.3; the deletion may be cryptic
cytogenetic_cases.typical_configuration: Often too small for a routine karyotype, or carried on a derivative
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: The chromosome 4 pair can look normal when the deletion is small
cytogenetic_cases.partner_note: None when the change is a cryptic deletion. A partner is involved in an unbalanced translocation.
example_notation: A normal-looking 46,XX or 46,XY does not exclude a cryptic 4p deletion
cytogenetic_cases.mechanism: Deletion or unbalanced rearrangement of 4p16.3 below reliable routine resolution
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not draw a shortened 4p for this case.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: The karyotype may look normal
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Partial monosomy 4p16.3 that may require FISH or a microarray

references.label: NCBI GeneReviews
references.citation: Battaglia A, Carey JC, South ST. Wolf-Hirschhorn syndrome. GeneReviews. Bookshelf ID NBK1183. Retired chapter, retained as the cited source: diagnosis uses the 4p16.3 critical region; conventional karyotyping detects only a portion of deletions, and smaller deletions need FISH or chromosomal microarray.

references.label: ISCN
references.citation: McGowan-Jordan J, Hastings RJ, Moore S, eds. ISCN 2020: An International System for Human Cytogenomic Nomenclature. Basel: Karger; 2020.

diseases.teaching_notes: Chronic myeloid leukemia is the disease. The simple lab uses the visible t(9;22) and asks the student to follow both derivative chromosomes. A cryptic or complex BCR::ABL1 rearrangement is a different case.

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: t(9;22)(q34;q11.2), with der(22) as the Philadelphia chromosome.
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: One chromosome 9 and one chromosome 22 are derivative chromosomes. der(22) is the small Philadelphia chromosome.
cytogenetic_cases.material_added: None. 9q material is on der(22), and 22q material is on der(9).
cytogenetic_cases.mechanism: Reciprocal translocation joining ABL1 and BCR
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not describe this as an abnormality of chromosome 22 alone.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: Pieces of 9q and 22q have exchanged. der(22) is the Philadelphia chromosome.
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: t(9;22)(q34;q11.2) producing BCR::ABL1. der(22) is the Philadelphia chromosome.

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: BCR::ABL1 without the classic visible t(9;22).
cytogenetic_cases.homolog_affected: The fusion can be present when chromosomes 9 and 22 look normal, or when additional chromosomes are involved
cytogenetic_cases.specific_region: 9q34 and 22q11.2, sometimes in a complex or insertion rearrangement
cytogenetic_cases.structural_class: BCR::ABL1 fusion that is not the simple two-break t(9;22) drawing
cytogenetic_cases.typical_configuration: Not the classic der(9) and der(22) pair
cytogenetic_cases.whole_chromosome_count: Often 46, but a complex karyotype can have other changes
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: Chromosomes 9 and 22 may look normal
example_notation: BCR::ABL1 may require FISH or another assay when t(9;22) is not visible
cytogenetic_cases.mechanism: Cryptic insertion or complex rearrangement producing BCR::ABL1
cytogenetic_cases.derivative: A Philadelphia chromosome may not be recognizable
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not draw the classic der(22) for this case.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: A normal-looking pair 9 and pair 22 does not exclude BCR::ABL1
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: BCR::ABL1 without the classic visible Philadelphia chromosome

references.label: ISCN
references.citation: McGowan-Jordan J, Hastings RJ, Moore S, eds. ISCN 2020: An International System for Human Cytogenomic Nomenclature. Basel: Karger; 2020.

references.label: WHO
references.citation: Khoury JD, et al. The 5th edition of the World Health Organization classification of haematolymphoid tumours: myeloid and histiocytic/dendritic neoplasms. Leukemia. 2022;36:1703-1719.

diseases.teaching_notes: Acute promyelocytic leukemia is the disease. The simple lab uses t(15;17) with PML::RARA. Variant RARA rearrangements are a different case and are not this chromosome pair.

cytogenetic_cases.material_added: None. Each derivative carries material from the partner.
cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: t(15;17)(q24.1;q21.2), PML::RARA.
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: One chromosome 15 and one chromosome 17 are derivative chromosomes
cytogenetic_cases.mechanism: Reciprocal translocation joining PML and RARA
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not describe this as an abnormality of chromosome 17 alone.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: Pieces of 15q and 17q have exchanged. There is no single familiar small marker like the Philadelphia chromosome.
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: t(15;17)(q24.1;q21.2) producing PML::RARA

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: a RARA rearrangement that is not t(15;17).
cytogenetic_cases.homolog_affected: RARA is fused to a partner other than PML
cytogenetic_cases.specific_region: RARA, with a partner that is not chromosome 15
cytogenetic_cases.typical_configuration: Not der(15) and der(17) from t(15;17)
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: Chromosomes 15 and 17 are not the exchanged pair
cytogenetic_cases.material_missing: None. Material is rearranged with a different partner.
cytogenetic_cases.partner_note: The partner of RARA varies and is not chromosome 15
example_notation: The ISCN uses the actual partner of RARA, not t(15;17)
cytogenetic_cases.genes: RARA with a partner other than PML
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not draw t(15;17) for this case.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: Pair 15 and pair 17 are not the finding
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Variant RARA rearrangement, not PML::RARA from t(15;17)

references.label: NCBI Bookshelf
references.citation: Cingam SR, Koshy NV. Acute promyelocytic leukemia. StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing. Bookshelf ID NBK459352. Most APL has a PML::RARA rearrangement; variant RARA partners are a minority. The teaching breakpoint in this lab follows ISCN 2020, t(15;17)(q24.1;q21.2).

references.label: Clinical
references.citation: Sanz MA, Fenaux P, Tallman MS, et al. Management of acute promyelocytic leukemia: updated recommendations from an expert panel of the European LeukemiaNet. Blood. 2019;133(15):1630-1643.

references.label: ISCN
references.citation: McGowan-Jordan J, Hastings RJ, Moore S, eds. ISCN 2020. Basel: Karger; 2020. Includes the 15q24.1 band used for PML.

diseases.teaching_notes: Burkitt lymphoma is the disease. The simple lab uses t(8;14) with IGH::MYC. t(2;8) and t(8;22) are different MYC rearrangements.

cytogenetic_cases.material_added: None. Each derivative carries material from the partner.
cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: t(8;14)(q24;q32), IGH::MYC.
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: One chromosome 8 and one chromosome 14 are derivative chromosomes
cytogenetic_cases.mechanism: Reciprocal translocation joining MYC and IGH
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not describe this as an abnormality of chromosome 8 alone. t(2;8) and t(8;22) are different cases.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: Pieces of 8q and 14q have exchanged
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: t(8;14)(q24;q32) producing IGH::MYC

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: t(2;8), a MYC rearrangement with IGK.
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: Chromosome 14 is not the partner
cytogenetic_cases.mechanism: MYC rearrangement with an immunoglobulin light-chain locus on chromosome 2
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not draw t(8;14) for this case.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: The partner is chromosome 2, not chromosome 14
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Variant Burkitt translocation t(2;8)

cytogenetic_cases.patient_case_label: This patient's case: t(8;22), a MYC rearrangement with IGL.
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: Chromosome 14 is not the partner. This der(22) is not the Philadelphia chromosome.
cytogenetic_cases.mechanism: MYC rearrangement with an immunoglobulin light-chain locus on chromosome 22
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not draw t(8;14), and do not call this der(22) a Philadelphia chromosome.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: The partner is chromosome 22, not chromosome 14

cytogenetic_cases.typical_configuration: der(2) and der(5) in the canonical variant
cytogenetic_cases.visual_change: The canonical variant exchanges distal 2p and distal 5q
cytogenetic_cases.added: Distal 5q is on der(2). Distal 2p is on der(5).
cytogenetic_cases.partnerNote: Canonical partner only. Other ALK partners exist.
cytogenetic_cases.final_interpretation: Canonical variant t(2;5)(p23;q35), NPM1::ALK. Chromosome 2 breaks at p23 and chromosome 5 breaks at q35. Break-apart FISH shows ALK rearrangement and does not name NPM1.
cytogenetic_cases.mechanism: Canonical reciprocal translocation joining NPM1 and ALK. Other ALK partners occur.
cytogenetic_cases.genes: ALK at 2p23. Canonical partner NPM1 at 5q35; result NPM1::ALK. Break-apart FISH does not identify the partner.
cytogenetic_cases.doNot: Do not imply every ALK-positive lymphoma has t(2;5).
cytogenetic_cases.notice: The canonical variant is t(2;5), with breakpoints at 2p23 and 5q35. The break-apart question is whether ALK is rearranged.

diseases.teaching_notes: t(11;22)(q24;q12), EWSR1::FLI1, is the canonical teaching mechanism. Conventional karyotyping is not the primary activity. Chromosome analysis shows the canonical breakpoints. FISH is an EWSR1 break-apart assay and does not prove the partner is FLI1.

cytogenetic_cases.homolog_affected: One chromosome 11 and one chromosome 22 in the canonical variant
cytogenetic_cases.material_added: 11q material is on der(22). 22q material is on der(11).
cytogenetic_cases.partner_note: Canonical partner only. EWSR1 has other partners.
cytogenetic_cases.do_not_alter: Do not treat an EWSR1 break-apart result as proof that the partner is FLI1.
cytogenetic_cases.student_should_notice: The canonical breakpoints are 11q24 and 22q12. The FISH question is whether EWSR1 is rearranged.
